svg.title: Cardiac fibrosis: a cellular overview
svg.desc: A concise editable 16:9 light-mode overview matching the previous cell-type visual abstracts. Four cards summarize endothelial cells, fibroblasts, macrophages/monocytes and cardiomyocytes with three key points each. A central circular panel presents three selected interaction themes: macrophage-to-fibroblast activation, cardiomyocyte-to-endothelial vascular growth, and cardiomyocyte–fibroblast inhibitory control. Connectors indicate participation in the network, not additional causal pathways. Sixteen numbered DOI references are clickable and have full citation tooltips.

svg.text: Four cell types and three interaction themes that shape injury, scar formation and repair

g.title: Endothelial cells: Perfusion and vascular repair. Maintain the microvascular bed and mount angiogenic responses. Immune regulation. Control leukocyte trafficking and inflammatory communication. Injury-induced plasticity. Transient mesenchymal programs do not establish fibroblast fate.
g.text: Maintain the microvascular bed and mount angiogenic responses.
Control leukocyte trafficking and inflammatory communication.
Transient mesenchymal programs do not establish fibroblast fate.

g.title: Fibroblasts: Main matrix-producing cells. Resident fibroblasts expand and remodel ECM after injury. Multiple activation states. Proliferation, myofibroblast activity and scar maturation differ. Signals and mechanics tune output. TGF-β and mechanical cues regulate matrix production.
g.text: Resident fibroblasts expand and remodel ECM after injury.
Proliferation, myofibroblast activity and scar maturation differ.
TGF-β and mechanical cues regulate matrix production.

g.title: Monocytes / macrophages: Clear damage and support repair. Remove dying cells and cardiomyocyte mitochondrial cargo. Tune fibroblast and vascular responses. Secreted signals can support healing or sustain fibrosis. Origin and state matter. Resident and recruited populations have context-specific roles.
g.text: Remove dying cells and cardiomyocyte mitochondrial cargo.
Secreted signals can support healing or sustain fibrosis.
Resident and recruited populations have context-specific roles.

g.title: Cardiomyocytes: Injury initiates remodeling. Cell loss triggers scar repair; chronic stress changes signaling. Stress contributes to dysfunction. Oxidative damage and senescence promote adverse remodeling. The environment shapes function. Fibroblast signals and matrix changes alter muscle performance.
g.text: Cell loss triggers scar repair; chronic stress changes signaling.
Oxidative damage and senescence promote adverse remodeling.
Fibroblast signals and matrix changes alter muscle performance.

g.title: Three selected intercellular mechanisms: macrophage CCL24/CCR3 and monocyte HB-EGF/EGFR activate fibroblasts; CM ZEB2-dependent TMSB4/PTMA supports endothelial growth; CM EV miR24 restrains fibroblast activation while fibroblast HTRA3 limits ambient TGF-beta activity. These are findings from different experimental systems, not a combined pathway or treatment regimen.

svg.text: Cell state, tissue location and timing shape the balance between effective repair and persistent remodeling.
Selected findings from the supplied cell-type and interaction tables; evidence spans human observations, cell models and animal perturbations.
CM: cardiomyocyte; FB: fibroblast; EC: endothelial cell; ECM: extracellular matrix; EV: extracellular vesicle.
